content: Potassium lactate is a chemical compound with the molecular formula KC3H5O3, or structurally represented as H3C-CHOH-COOK. It is the potassium salt derived from lactic acid. This compound is synthesized by neutralizing lactic acid, which itself is produced through the fermentation of a sugar source. Potassium lactate is assigned the E number E326 for its use in food applications. Typically, potassium lactate is available as a liquid product containing approximately 60% solids, though it can be formulated with up to 78% solids. It is widely utilized in the food industry, particularly in meat and poultry products, to enhance shelf life and improve food safety. This is due to its broad-spectrum antimicrobial properties, which make it effective in inhibiting the growth of most spoilage and pathogenic bacteria. In addition to its role in food preservation, potassium lactate is also employed as an extinguishing agent in certain fire suppression systems, such as the First Alert Tundra fire extinguishers.
